description:
We are AeroAcoustic, a three-member team competing in The Earth Information Jukebox challenge! Combining our backgrounds in software development, data analysis, and creative design, we are building an interactive experience that translates NASA's Earth science visualizations into rich, expressive sound and music.

Our goal is to make complex climate and atmospheric data engaging, intuitive, and accessible to everyone—including visually impaired audiences—through the power of data sonification.
summary: SoniSphere is an interactive Earth observation web platform that converts NASA Earth Information Center satellite and simulation datasets into real-time, synchronized soundscapes and 3D visuals. Addressing the Earth Information Jukebox challenge, it uses computer vision and Web Audio synthesis to mathematically map physical measurements—including GEOS atmospheric CO2, VIIRS decadal night lights, ECCO2 ocean currents, and ISS lightning—into calibrated acoustic dimensions such as frequency, spatial pan, and harmonic tension. Instead of arbitrary background music, SoniSphere functions as a transparent scientific instrument featuring synchronized 3D WebGL globes and a real-time telemetry panel, providing a multi-sensory, accessible interface for climate researchers, educators, and visually impaired users to perceive planetary changes through sound.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?


SoniSphere is an open-access, browser-based Earth observation platform that converts multi-petabyte NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) datasets into synchronized real-time audio, dynamic 3D WebGL globes, and scientific telemetry. Rather than playing pre-recorded background music, SoniSphere operates as a procedural data-to-sound synthesizer: every sound wave heard is generated live by mathematical functions driven directly by satellite pixels.
  • DYAMOND Global CO2 (GEOS 3D Model): Global CO2​ levels (407–421 ppm) control a continuous gliding bass drone (65 Hz to 261 Hz)—as greenhouse gases rise, the planet’s pitch rises. Continental plumes are spatialized across stereo headphones: Americas on the Left (Marimba), Europe/Africa in Center (Cello), and East Asia on the Right (Celesta).

  • Decadal Night Lights (VIIRS Black Marble): Measures 10 years of global electrification. Pristine baseline areas produce warm, calm tones, while growing cities trigger ascending melodic arpeggios with bright acoustic filters.

  • ISS Lightning Sensor (LIS): Converts orbital thunderstorm flashes into real-time percussive transients over an orbital carrier drone.
  • ECCO2 Ocean Currents: Translates oceanic flow velocity and heat circulation into deep sub-bass frequencies and kinetic ocean swells.

What benefits does it have?

  • Instant Pattern Recognition: The human ear detects sudden changes, rhythm spikes, and microtonal shifts much faster than eyes can scan complex graphs.
  • Explainable Sound: Every sound is backed by an on-screen "Explain the Sound" panel showing exact values (ppm, Hz, decibels, stereo pan), ensuring complete scientific transparency.
  • Zero-Latency In-Browser Audio: Procedural synthesis runs directly in the user’s browser—no heavy audio files to download, loading instantaneously on any device.

What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Universal Accessibility: Earth science relies heavily on visual maps and color scales that exclude blind and low-vision communities. SoniSphere turns satellite data into an intuitive auditory experience.
  • Public Climate Awareness: Hearing the fundamental pitch of our atmosphere physically rise as CO2 accumulates makes climate change visceral, immediate, and understandable to everyone.
  • Classroom & Research Tool: Gives educators an engaging multi-sensory teaching tool and gives researchers a way to monitor multi-year planetary data streams through sound.

What tools, coding languages, and software were used?

  • Frontend: Next.js 15 (React 19), Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons
  • 3D Graphics: Three.js (WebGL interactive Earth globes with dynamic atmosphere shaders)
  • Real-time Audio: Tone.js & native Web Audio API (procedural synthesizers, spatial panners, dynamic filters)
  • Data Preprocessing: Python, OpenCV (cv2), NumPy (automated frame extraction and color-space telemetry extraction)
  • Testing & Quality: Python unittest suite

How is our project creative?

  • Planetary Binaural Soundstage: We mapped global longitudes directly to stereo hearing—listeners wearing headphones can locate where emissions are happening on Earth purely by ear (West to East).
  • Continuous Pitch Gliding (Portamento): Atmospheric gases don't move in rigid musical steps; our CO2\text{CO}_2CO2​ drone glides smoothly across fractional frequencies to authentically mirror fluid dynamics.
  • Multi-Sensory Synchronization: A single plume surge simultaneously brightens the 2D map, illuminates the 3D globe’s atmosphere, and triggers a localized pitch swell in audio.

What factors did our team consider?

  • Acoustic Comfort: Raw data sonification can quickly sound harsh. We shaped envelopes and tuned resonant filters to eliminate distortion and crackling, creating an ambient, comfortable listening experience.
  • Scientific Accuracy: Sound parameters were strictly calibrated to real peer-reviewed baselines rather than arbitrary musical choices.
  • Cross-Device Performance: Optimized 3D textures and lightweight client-side audio ensure smooth 60 FPS performance on standard laptops and mobile phones without draining bandwidth.
